A Jew told Umar that had the verse perfecting the religion come to them they would celebrate its day; Umar said it came on a Friday at Arafat.
When Gabriel did not come for a time and a Quraysh woman said his Satan had left him, revelation came that his Lord had neither forsaken nor hated him.
Ibn Abbas explains that in verse 49.13 Shu'ub means the large nations and Qabail the branch tribes.
Ibn Umar said the verse 'whether you show what is in your minds or conceal it' was abrogated by the verse following it.
Jabir said the verse about two parties about to lose heart, with Allah their Protector, concerned Banu Haritha and Banu Salama, and they were glad it was revealed.
Reciting the verse excepting weak men, women and children, Ibn Abbas said he and his mother were among the weak Muslims at Mecca whom Allah excused.
Ikrima forbade joining an army against Sham, citing Muslims killed while swelling the pagans' numbers against the Prophet; Ibn Abbas said his mother was among the excused weak.
Ibn Abbas said the verse allowing for the inconvenience of rain or illness was revealed concerning Abdur-Rahman bin Auf, who was wounded.
Umar told Jews who would have celebrated its day that 'This day I have perfected your religion' came down on the day of Arafat while he was there.
Ibn Abbas said the deaf and dumb called the worst of beasts in the verse were some people of Bani Abd-ad-Dar.
Ibn Masud said that before Islam, when a tribe grew numerous, people said 'amira' of it.
Ibn Abbas explains that 'will bring you home' in verse 28.85 means to Mecca.
Marwan claims the verse on one who says 'Fie' to his parents was revealed about Abdur-Rahman bin Abu Bakr, and Aisha replies nothing was revealed about them but her innocence.
Asked who the others in verse 62.3 are, the Prophet puts his hand on Salman and says men of his people would reach faith even at the Pleiades.
Ibn Abbas says verse 68.13 was revealed about a man of Quraysh marked by a sign like the one hung on a sheep's neck.
Surat al-Mursalat was revealed to the Prophet in a cave as a snake escaped them, and Ibn Abbas explains its sparks like Al-Qasr by the logs they stored.
Ibn Abbas says 'from stage to stage' in the verse means from one state to another, and concerns the Prophet.
In a sermon the Prophet explains 91.12 on the man who hamstrung the she-camel, warns against lashing one's wife like a slave, and against laughing at breaking wind.
After Surat an-Nasr came down the Prophet glorified Allah and asked forgiveness in his prayers, and Ibn Abbas tells Umar the surah informed the Prophet his death was near.
A Jew told Umar his people would have made a festival of the day the verse perfecting the religion came, and Umar said it came on Arafat day, a Friday.
The verse against praying too loud or too low told the Prophet, hiding in Mecca, to recite so companions but not pagans hear; Aisha said it concerned invocations.
